You can find the full project documentation (vision, architecture, annotation types, roadmap) [through this link](https://docs.annotrain.cmaslard.xyz/), the source code [at this link](https://github.com/cmaslard/AnnoTrain), and a shorter overview [on the tools page](https://cmaslard.xyz/tools/AnnoTrain.html).

AnnoTrain is an open platform for participatory scientific image annotation, deep learning, and education, built around four pillars: **participatory annotation, deep learning, education, and open science**. It connects the full scientific workflow, human annotation, dataset creation, model training, evaluation, sharing, reuse, and improvement, so that researchers can turn raw images into quality-controlled datasets and trained models, while students and other contributors can learn how human annotations become training data and how that data shapes model predictions and performance.

The platform is designed to make deep learning less of a "black box": contributors annotate images through a minimal-friction interface (open link → annotate → next image, no account required), and the resulting datasets can train baseline models whose predictions, uncertainty, and errors are then fed back to humans for correction, a human-in-the-loop loop that keeps improving both the dataset and the model over successive versions.

A first pedagogical prototype targets the *Bioinformatics Tools* MSc course at the University of Neuchâtel (session *A First Neural Network*, planned for November 2026), where \~40 students annotate camera-trap images and directly build the dataset used to train their first neural network. On the research side, the [DeepPlate](https://cmaslard.xyz/tools/DeepPlate.html) segmentation model is a target early use case for validating human-in-the-loop model improvement inside AnnoTrain.

🚧 AnnoTrain is currently under active early-stage development, see the [roadmap](https://docs.annotrain.cmaslard.xyz/roadmap/) for current progress.
